verdict.rationale: GitHub documents fine-grained personal access tokens. You grant each token a specific set of permissions that limit which resources it can reach through the API, which delivers scoped, least-privilege credentials an agent can use. The `X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions` response header also tells you the minimum permissions each endpoint needs, which helps keep tokens narrow. Missing for 10: evidence of per-repository scoping, token expiration or revocation controls, agent-specific credential guidance (e.g., GitHub App or installation tokens for agents), and independent or hands-on corroboration.
